correctness.rationale: Writing \(x=r+ps\) yields the exact stationary-point formula. Cubing permutes \(\mathbb F_p\), so a nonzero quartic frequency modulo \(p\) gives exactly one nonvanishing stationary contribution. Cyclotomic root-counting reduces frequencies divisible by \(p\) to permutation of \(Ax+Bx^4\). For \(p=6h+5\), the choices \(j=3\lceil h/2\rceil+1\) and \(k=2h+1-\lceil h/2\rceil\) yield a nonzero power-sum obstruction whenever \(B\ne0\), except cases with \(A=0\) where \(x^4\) is already noninjective. Therefore the complete Fourier-zero set is formula (1) of RESULT.md. Orthogonality then saturates all \(p\) residue classes and uniquely determines every spectrum. The \(p^{p+1}\) total and \(p^3\) affine subcount follow. Exact root-of-unity tests at \(p=5,11,17\) and moment checks through \(p=23\) corroborate, but do not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies every spectral frequency set for a natural quartic Fourier graph on an infinite arithmetic family of prime-square rings, with exact \(p^{p+1}\) enumeration, exactly \(p^3\) affine graph bases, and explicit nonlinear bases. The Hermite moment proof supplies the nontrivial arithmetic rigidity separating this setting from cubic and quadratic graph cases; this is a natural structural classification, not a routine finite table.
